<reason>CON won by steadily narrowing the debate to a single mechanism and forcing PRO to shrink its promise. CON's core move — that the reconnection request itself is a data disclosure that precedes the consent supposed to authorize it — was pressed in Rebuttal 1, sharpened into two precise pressure questions, and then PRO's A1/A2 answers ("public handles you already see cross first"; unfindable users get nothing) were turned into concessions: the "pseudonymous supporters" benefit was effectively withdrawn, and the residual gain was PRO's own "one click versus days of hunting." CON also offered a concrete alternative plan in direct answer to PRO's Q2 (portable posts and follow lists, protected departure notices, antitrust), which undercut PRO's "tenancy forever" framing, and CON correctly noted the motion binds every platform while PRO kept retreating to "gatekeepers only." PRO had a real live route — exit ramp/competition and the "strictly narrower than a public post" argument — and answered the pressure questions in proper format, but it never engaged CON's push-vs-passive distinction or the alternative plan, and its closing largely repeated earlier framing. CON's clipped first rebuttal is a real execution cost but the truncated point was already made in its opening. Both sides used plausible background knowledge without fake sourcing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Pressure Q1/Q2 followed by [B4.1]-[B4.6]: after PRO conceded that handles cross first and that unfindable contacts get nothing, CON reframed the entire mandate as "re-following with a notification," quoted PRO's own "one click vs. afternoon" as the sole gain, and weighed it against a compelled cross-platform roster — "consent that arrives after disclosure is not consent; it is notification."</best_rebuttal>
